 1h ago 17.40 EST And on that note … here is David Hynter’s report from Old Trafford. 
 Thanks for joining me.
 Manchester United produce comeback for the ages as Cunha double floors Roma Read more Share 1h ago 17.40 EST Michael Carrick: “It was a good night, I must give a lot of credit to the payers for character and to the supporters. I think we grew into it after giving goals too easily. The boys made everything of every little opportunity.
 “I told them to not get too disappointed, I thought we were coming into the game. It didn’t feel like that to the players who were carrying a lot of disappointed.
 “It’s one game, so it depends on what happens next. We need to capitalise on that. I thought Youri was fantastic and showed everything that he is. It was nice to see this place like that again.
 “I am delighted for Shea, he is so talented. He is well liked, the boys respect him a lot. To see young players take opportunities like that, there are not many better things.
 “Seeing the supporters going home happy is what we live for.
 “We’ve shown a lot of character as a group, I hope the players have found out a lot about me, I’ve found out a lot about them.”
 Share 1h ago 17.31 EST Over in Barcelona … 
 Raphinha underlines Barcelona’s class to give Aston Villa a reality check Read more Share Updated at  17.39 EST 1h ago 17.30 EST Kobbie Mainoo: “It was unbelievable, it was the magic of this stadium and club to come from two goals down. We needed a bit of a kick, we were a bit reactionary. The boss really drilled into us that we needed to be more active and take the game.
 “We know what we are capable of and are dangerous team, it is all about getting the to come together. Everyone is buzzing."
 Share 2h ago 17.14 EST Some honest and meaningful words from Fernandes there. Strong but honest words. He also offered up a late swear.
 Share 2h ago 17.13 EST Bruno Fernandes: “It’s tough to say something, it’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to perform the way we want. We have not been consistent. Today was important to get a win. We knew after half time we still had the fans with us and we could change it with a goal. Fortunately we did.
 “IN the first one it didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong with the way I prepared. I cleared my head and scored.
 “It’s been tough for the fans but having their belief helps the side. Today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive and we made Roma experience that.
 “It is about performing and getting results at this club. It’s been a long time without a win, it’s been frustrating for them and us too. The fans want to win games, they are used to seeing this club at the top. We are frustrated with the situation at the moment and hopefully this win is the start of something good.
 “We don’t need to save anyone’s job. The club and the players needed that win. The situation has been tough, there have been a lot of lies in the media. The manager made a decision to put me on the bench because of my performances, that’s fair. People thought it was a punishment for the words I said and if it was, he was right, the manager is the one who makes the decision and I have to agree with that.”
 View image in fullscreen You can see what Matheus Cunha’s third goal meant to Bruno Fernandes. Photograph: Richard Sellers/Allstar Picture Library/Sportsphoto Share Updated at  17.45 EST 2h ago 17.08 EST Youri Tielemans: “It is brilliant. The fans were brilliant. Tonight the turnaround was brilliant. We were on the front foot in the second half and we succeeded. There has been a lot of pressure on the manager and we paid him back with a comeback. All we can do is stick behind him and support him.
 “At the end of the say we are on the pitch, we need to show what we are capable of.
 “Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and we can build on this.”
 Share 2h ago 17.04 EST I feel I enjoyed a nice few moments of calm there to recover after the silliness of all that soccer. 
 Share 2h ago 16.57 EST Surely this means my day off is safe … 
 Share 2h ago 16.57 EST Cunha is arguing with a United official about something or other. 
 I wonder if he’s not allowed back on the pitch after being sent off.
 Share 2h ago 16.56 EST Joshua Keeling ponders : “Matheus Robins?”
 Share 2h ago 16.56 EST Berrada and Wilcox are not giving much away with their emotions in the stands. I suspect they are just as confused as everyone else.
 Share 2h ago 16.55 EST Full time: Manchester United 3-2 Roma
 How on earth did that happen? It looked like a completely different United team after the break. The first 45 minutes was complete and utter mediocrity but they were resurgent, re-energise and fought back. They were fortunate with the retaken penalty and the equalise but heard hard work earned that, before Cunha’s stunning winner.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United manager Michael Carrick and Youri Tieleman are all smiles after the final whistle. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA Share Updated at  17.12 EST 2h ago 16.53 EST 90+4 mins: Cristante lifts a cross to the back post for Castro, who heads well wide.
 Share 2h ago 16.52 EST 90+3 mins: The United fans return to chants of wanting the Glazers out.
 Share 2h ago 16.52 EST 90+2 mins: Can United hold on with 10 men?!
 Roma are looking for an opening but the hosts have gone very deep.
 Mbeumo is fouled when taking the ball up the pitch and is happy to be so.
 Share 2h ago 16.51 EST RED CARD! Cunha
 90+1 mins: United are still pressing and putting in the effort but Cunha is overzealous and crashes into a defender. He is given a second booking; his first came for celebrating the third goal.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Matheus Cunha sits in front of the fans after being shown a red card. Photograph: Jon Super/AP Share Updated at  17.03 EST 2h ago 16.50 EST 90 mins: Five minutes added on.
 Share 2h ago 16.49 EST 89 mins: The fans are chanting Carrick’s name now.
 Kevin Wilson writes: “Lacey has turned the game. Maybe trust the kids, Michael.”
 Share 2h ago 16.48 EST 88 mins: CAN UNITED HOLD ON?! Is the new question.
 De Ligt and Mount are coming on. Maguire and Fernandes off.
 Share 2h ago 16.46 EST GOAL! A stunning pass from Lacey finds Cunha inside the box, he takes a touch and then hits the ball with the ferocity of a very angry man to beat the goalkeeper at the near post. The Brazilian then dives into the crowd and everyone is loving it.
 View image in fullscreen Matheus Cunha slaps the ball home for his second and Manchester United’s third goal of the night. Photograph: Conor Molloy/ProSports/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Scenes! Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters Share Updated at  16.58 EST 2h ago 16.45 EST GOAL! Manchester United 3-2 Roma (Cunha, 86)
 RUDDY HELL! 
 Share 2h ago 16.44 EST 85 mins: Castro and Maguire are down inside the Roma half after a coming together.
 Share 2h ago 16.44 EST 84 mins: I think it is far to say this has been a game of two halves. Roma were dominant in the first, United in the second. Will we get a dramatic end?
 Share 2h ago 16.43 EST GOAL! Manchester United 2-2 Roma (Cunha, 83)
 Cunha profits from a dreadful defensive mistake from Balerdi to score from close range.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Matheus Cunha scores their second goal. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Cunha celebrates restoring parity. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  17.06 EST 2h ago 16.42 EST 82 mins: Lacey is looking to take Wesley on whenever he gets the ball.
 Share 2h ago 16.41 EST 81 mins: United offer some promise going forward but it all falls down on the edge of the box.
 Share 2h ago 16.38 EST 79 mins: Castro battles with Maguire and catches an arm in the face, which the referee deems is worthy of a foul and booking for the United defender.
 Share 2h ago 16.37 EST 78 mins: Malen off, Castro on for Roma .
 Share 2h ago 16.37 EST 77 mins: United look a threat from set-pieces, so maybe should try and work a way of winning more corners.
 In the meantime, Cunha forces the goalkeeper into a decent save with a shot from distance. Lacey picks up the loose ball and defeats Wesley, getting a cross in, only to be taken down by the wing-back. United want a penalty but the officials are having none of it.
 Share 2h ago 16.35 EST 75 mins: Martinez and Lacey are coming on. The Argentinian gets a mixed reception as he replaces Heaven, while the academy graduate is cheered as Diallo goes off.
 Roma take off Mancini and Hermoso, Ndicka and Ghilardi on.
 Share 2h ago 16.34 EST 74 mins: The game has become a little bit scrappy in the past two minutes. Carrick has readied Martinez …
 Share 2h ago 16.32 EST 72 mins: Everything was going so well, and then Dalot falls over to give away a throw.
 Share 2h ago 16.30 EST 71 mins: Cunha wins the ball on the right and drives at Balerdi who takes it off his toes.
 Share 3h ago 16.29 EST 70 mins: There’s something akin to a zip about United at the moment.
 That is briefly halted by Heaven being penalised for a foul and then booked.
 Share 3h ago 16.28 EST 68 mins: Another corner! Mbeumo lifts it to the back post where Maguire is battling to get on the end of it, having got the better of Balerdi, but he can’t get his effort on target.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Harry Maguire heads at goal. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Maguire rues his miss. Photograph: Steve Taylor/PPAUK/Shutterstock Share Updated at  16.37 EST 3h ago 16.27 EST 67 mins: Mbeumo swings in a second corner from the right, which is headed back across goal for Dalot to nod towards the net, only to it cleared off the line.
 Share 3h ago 16.26 EST 66 mins: United have a corner on the left for Fernandes to whip in. It reaches Maguire at the back post but his header is blocked by Wesley.
 One key issue for United is a lack of options on the bench. Carrick could bring on Lacey, Mount or Zirkzee if he wants an attacking option but it’s not the most exciting thought.
 Share 3h ago 16.24 EST 65 mins: United are moving at greater speed, going from one end of the pitch to the other. It catches Roma out and gives Dalot a chance but he hits the side netting.
 United go back at Roma and Fernandes finds Diallo in the box, he cuts in but his shot is blocked. United are on top here.
 Share 3h ago 16.22 EST 63 mins: Obviously, we should also remember the wider Champions League context because a loss here would mean it is three defeats in four for United in the competition.
 Share 3h ago 16.20 EST 61 mins: United need to build on this because they have half an hour to save the manager’s job, I would argue. The fans are doing their bit.
 Share 3h ago 16.19 EST 59 mins: Cunha sends the ball through for Mbeumo who reaches it first and takes aim. His shot defeats the goalkeeper but comes back after hitting both posts. Old Trafford is rocking now.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Bryan Mbeumo beats the keeper but not the woodwork. Photograph: Jon Super/AP Share Updated at  16.29 EST 3h ago 16.18 EST GOAL! Manchester United 1-2 Roma (Fernandes, pen, 58)
 Like a bit of drama, do you? Fernandes scores at the second time of asking.
 View image in fullscreen Back of the net … Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA View image in fullscreen And back in the game. Photograph: Richard Sellers/Allstar Picture Library/Sportsphoto Share Updated at  16.33 EST 3h ago 16.17 EST PENALTY RETAKE!
 The Roma players are adjudged to have encroached!
 Share 3h ago 16.16 EST Penalty saved!
 Fernandes sends the penalty to the goalkeeper’s right and Vasquez gets down to save. The rebound is then cleared.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes has a penalty saved by Roma goalkeeper Devis Vasquez. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at  16.35 EST 3h ago 16.16 EST 56 mins: VAR is having a good look … does Cunha trip himself up? Fernandes has the ball in his hand as United wait for a final verdict. Penalty given.
 Share 3h ago 16.14 EST 55 mins: PENALTY TO UNITED! Cunha is bundled over in the box by Mancini. The Brazilian then demands some passion from the crowd.
